correctness.rationale: A length-k prefix has Frobenius normal length sqrt(k), so intersecting the shifted halfspaces characterizes every radius-r center. For m<=n, the n first-row entry lower bounds and the first-row total upper bound give (n+sqrt(n))r<=1. The constant matrix attains equality; equality forces the whole first row and, when square, the first column. The explicit perturbations in RESULT.md lines 50–52 give strict slack in every genuinely unforced inequality, proving the affine dimensions and showing that the listed universal contacts are the only contacts at every relative-interior center. At the constant center only length-one lowers and length-max(m,n) uppers can tie. Deduplicating the top-left lower constraint and checking the distinct facets gives the claimed counts. The wording about uniqueness in line 32 means that the optimal center is not unique, not that an individual ball lacks a unique geometric center.
